title: Chapter 39 — The Seven Closing Techniques for the Retail Floor
intro: The complete closing toolkit — seven techniques and the floor moments each one fits.

sections.title: The Direct Close
sections.content: Simply ask. 'Shall I write this up for you?' Works when the customer has shown clear buying signals — nodding, asking about delivery, checking their calendar.

sections.title: The Assumptive Close
sections.content: Act as if the decision is made. 'I will get this reserved. Does Tuesday or Thursday work better for delivery?' Skip the 'are you ready' question entirely.

sections.title: The Summary Close
sections.content: Recap everything they told you they wanted. 'So we have the 36-inch Bosch dishwasher at 42 decibels, the third rack for your wine glasses, and the stainless panel to match your kitchen — I have delivery available next Thursday. Let me get the paperwork started.'

sections.title: The Choice Close
sections.content: Give them two yeses. 'Would you like the standard installation or the premium with the water line hookup?' Either answer moves forward.

sections.title: The Urgency Close
sections.content: Use only when real: 'This promotion ends Sunday and the rebate is $200 — I want to make sure you get that.' Never fabricate urgency. If there is no promotion, do not invent one.

sections.title: The Package Close
sections.content: 'If we do the range, the hood, and the dishwasher together, I can sharpen the pricing on the package. Want me to see what I can do?' Multi-unit deals have higher margins and higher customer retention.

sections.title: When Not to Close
sections.content: If they have not seen the product demonstrated, if they have an unaddressed objection, if they seem confused or overwhelmed — back up to the step you skipped. The close should feel like the natural conclusion, not a surprise attack.
